subject: [PATCH 3/3] iova: defer maple tree erase on GFP_ATOMIC failure

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that freeing the iova when in-place store fails would leave the maple tree with a dangling pointer and proposes to return early and warn or panic instead.
reviews.raw_body:
If the in-place store fails, then updating
deferred_lo / hi won't help, since the
sweep later on will be unable to identify
this area.

Freeing the iova at that point would leave
the maple tree with a pointer into memory
that could be re-used for something else.

We need to either return early and warn,
or panic.

I'm fine with either.

Robin, do you have a preference here?

2026-06-26.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where removing an entry from the maple tree, used by the IOVA allocator, can fail under memory pressure due to GFP_ATOMIC allocation failures. To mitigate this issue, the patch introduces a deferred erase mechanism that overwrites the slot in place with a marker (IOVA_DEFERRED) and frees the struct iova immediately when the GFP_ATOMIC erase fails. The deferred erase is retried by the next allocation or successful free operation via the iova_drain_deferred() function. This approach keeps the struct iova at 16 bytes, avoiding the need for a per-iova list node and associated overhead. The patch also includes test cases to exercise the deferred-erase path.
